summary: Console alert duplication and incorrect attribution after hourly retention compaction
description:
Issue summary:
Customer KappaHealth reported multiple duplicate alert notifications for the same console rule over a four-hour window after our hourly retention compaction job ran. Alerts were emitted with different attribution metadata (org/route/model) and caused duplicated paging to their on-call.

Impact:
- Several duplicate P1 alerts sent to KappaHealth on-call (SMS + PagerDuty) between 02:00–06:00 UTC on 2026-03-10.
- Noise led to escalation and temporary disruption of their incident response.
- Affects alert evaluation and attribution reports in Console for orgs with high-cardinality tags.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1), console and alerting clusters behind ALB.
- Retention compaction job v2.3.1 (daily/hourly rollups) ran at 02:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) On a high-cardinality org with many tag permutations, enable a per-route 5m error-rate alert with 1m evaluation window.
2) Allow ingest and alerting to run across an hourly retention compaction boundary.
3) Observe alert eval log entries and notification dispatch records for duplicate IDs with differing attribution fields.

Observed behavior:
- Two or more alerts created for the same condition within a short span after compaction completes.
- Alert objects have different attribution fields (route_id vs. fallback_route) and different timebucket keys, causing duplicate evaluation paths.

Expected behavior:
- Single alert evaluation result per incident, with stable attribution preserved across retention compaction.

Initial workaround offered to customer:
- We suggested temporarily disabling hourly compaction for their org (not recommended long-term) and narrow the alert to use a route_id whitelist to ensure single attribution.
- Advised they mute duplicate PagerDuty escalations until we provide a permanent fix.

comments: 2026-03-10 03:10 - Support (Ava): Customer reported duplicate alerts. Collected org id and sample alert ids. Escalated to SRE for investigation.

2026-03-10 05:01 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced locally with a synthetic high-cardinality load. Saw duplicate alert evals around compaction boundary. Suspect compaction produces transient overlapping timebuckets used by evaluation engine.

2026-03-10 08:27 - Engineering (Priya, alerting): Confirmed compaction v2.3.1 writes compacted timebucket keys in place but does not update in-flight evaluation cache; causes duplicate eval paths on next evaluation cycle.

2026-03-11 09:22 - Support (Ava) to customer: Provided temporary mute guidance and request to postpone compaction during their peak hours. Customer accepted temporary mitigation while we work on a fix.

2026-03-12 14:40 - Engineering (Diego): Implemented a hypotheses test: added a per-transaction guard to dedupe evaluations by alert fingerprint and timebucket. Observed reduced duplicates in staging. Preparing PR for hotfix.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Engineering (Diego): Hotfix PR opened and running integration tests. Requesting on-call approval for a canary deploy to prod at low-traffic window (03:00 UTC).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Retention compaction rewrites timebucket keys while alert evaluation cache references stale keys, leading to duplicated evaluation runs.
Hypothesis 2: Notification dispatcher dedup key uses a timebucket-derived hash; if compaction changes bucket boundaries, the hash mutates and loses dedup protection.

Evidence: Repro script produced two evaluation records with same eval_id but different attribution_key and two distinct dispatch_ids. Alerting service metrics show a spike in 'eval_path_count' during compaction window.
Correlated with rc-20260310-02 compaction run. No prior similar reports before v2.3.1 rollout (rolled 2026-02-28).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: Customer muted PagerDuty integration for the affected rule and scheduled compaction postponement for their org during their peak window.

Planned fix: Engineering to ship hotfix that ensures evaluation cache invalidation post-compaction and strong deduplication on notification dispatcher based on stable alert fingerprint. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/824 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/1902.
Canary plan: Deploy hotfix to 10% of alerting traffic in us-east-1 during 03:00 UTC low-traffic window, monitor 'duplicate_alert_rate' and 'notify_latency' for 2 hours, then roll to 100% if stable.

Post-mortem actions: Update retention compaction runbook to include evaluation-cache invalidation step; add an integration test that simulates compaction boundary and validates no duplicate notifications.
